problem_statement: The Nuxt 3 Awesome Starter documentation site is a multi-page Nuxt 3 docs template — a home overview, an About-the-docs page, a Components docs page, and Blank/Test/Setting pages, all wrapped by a shared navbar and footer under the page layout. The starter ships its own built-in component library (Button, Link, Action Sheet, Card, Tabs, Text Input, Switch, Alert Banner). The docs team wants a small, consistent 'Browse the component library' panel to sit in the footer of every page: a category filter chip row (All / Actions / Layout / Forms / Feedback) over a grid of the starter's real components plus a live 'Showing N of 8' readout that names how many components the current filter shows — a reader clicks a category to narrow the list, so the readout should always name the live count and category. Ship the panel so it (1) appears in the footer on the home, About, Components docs, Blank, Test and Setting pages alike, (2) lays out its chip row and component grid responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the site's quiet slate/gray minimalist styling (bordered slate chips and tiles, not an off-palette dark slab), and (4) keeps the 'Showing N of 8' readout in sync with the filter so a reader who clicks the Forms category sees the readout update to 'Showing 2 of 8 · Forms'. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, existing page content, the static build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Browse the component library' panel to the site footer so it renders on the home, About, Components docs, Blank, Test and Setting pages (a shared component invoked from Footer.vue, not a per-page copy).

The panel shows a 'Browse the component library' label, a category filter chip row (All / Actions / Layout / Forms / Feedback), a grid of the starter's real components (Button, Link, Action Sheet, Card, Tabs, Text Input, Switch, Alert Banner) each tagged with its category, and a live 'Showing N of 8' readout.
The chip row and component grid must wrap responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the panel in the site's quiet slate/gray minimalist language (bordered slate chips and tiles), consistent and legible, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the 'Showing N of 8' readout to the category filter: after clicking a category chip, the readout must reflect the live filtered count and category (e.g. clicking Forms yields 'Showing 2 of 8 · Forms'), never a stale count.
author_notes: Built on the viandwi24 nuxt3-awesome-starter Nuxt 3 documentation theme (a shared navbar and footer under the page layout, a minimalist Tailwind slate/gray palette, a themed component library and color-mode support). The shared 'Browse the component library' panel lists the starter's OWN built-in components (components/awesome/* — Button, Link, Action Sheet, Card, Tabs, Text Input, Switch, Alert Banner) with a native category filter, and is rendered from Footer.vue as the LayoutPageDocsRail component; no remote assets are added — the original Google Fonts Nunito @import was dropped in favour of the system sans-serif fallback so the static Nuxt build is fully offline with zero console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the component-library panel as a shared component rendered from the footer so a single source of truth reaches every page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row and component grid must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so they never force horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the spacing must stay legible.

The panel must adopt the site's slate/gray palette, bordered-chip/tile style and minimalist typography so it reads as part of the docs site, not a foreign block; keep it consistent with the site's imagery.
The 'Showing N of 8' readout must reflect the CURRENT filter after every chip click by re-reading the live visible-tile count, so it can never go stale relative to the visible grid.
Do not remove or regress the navbar, footer, existing page content or the static Nuxt build; keep the site free of console and network errors.

change_completion: The component-library panel is present in the footer of the home, About, Components docs, Blank, Test and Setting pages (the shared component reaches every route).

After clicking the Forms category chip on the home page, the 'Showing N of 8' readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 8 · Forms' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 8 of 8 · All components'.
design_consistency: The panel on the footer states matches the reference's slate/gray minimalist styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette dark slab.
The panel adopts the site's slate bordered-chip/tile idiom so it reads as part of the docs site across every page.
responsive: No captured page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row and component grid wrap.
desktop_footer_home, mobile_footer_home and mobile_initial keep the component-library panel readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (Home/About/Components/Setting), the footer and the page headers remain present and functional.
The existing home/About/docs/Setting content and the static Nuxt build are not removed or broken; the site stays free of console and network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the home overview and the responsive shell.
desktop_docs, mobile_docs, desktop_about, mobile_about and desktop_setting protect the existing docs pages and carry the component-library panel in the footer.
desktop_footer_home and mobile_footer_home scroll the component-library panel into view and must show the slate/gray panel without horizontal overflow.
desktop_footer_docs and desktop_footer_setting protect the panel's presence on the Components docs and Setting page footers (the cross-page rollout).
toggle_mode_home clicks the Forms category chip; the 'Showing N of 8' readout must then read 'Showing 2 of 8 · Forms'.
